To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a color difference between sets is sufficient for a subset selective search; (ii) the effect of a color difference is additive with the number of irrelevant items in the irrelevant set and (iii) the effect of irrelevant items is not influenced by a color difference; (iv) the effect of the relevant items on search efficiency is modulated by a color difference between the sets, but only when the relevant items are defined by a unique color.
a preview reduces the influence of the irrelevant set when the irrelevant and relevant sets are presented simultaneously and differ in color but not when the two sets are presented sequentially.
a preview of irrelevant distractors reduces their influence on search efficiency in a feature search but not in a conjunction search.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new approach to the study of selective attention in visual search, and the results are in agreement with the view that preview search and color search are based on distinct mechanisms of selective attention.
the role of preview and color in subset selective search and contributes to the understanding of how these factors interact in determining search performance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
preview search is a complex phenomenon that depends on the specific combination of task demands.
preview search is a function of the subset size and color difference between subsets and the nature of the target.

a preview reduces the influence of the irrelevant set when the target is defined by a unique element within the relevant set, but that a preview does not reduce the influence of the relevant set when the target requires a conjunction of features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a color difference between irrelevant and relevant sets is an efficient means to reduce the influence of the irrelevant set, and that a preview is an efficient means when the target is defined by a unique relevant feature.
preview reduces the number of irrelevant distractors in the absence but does not reduce the number of relevant distractors in the presence of color.
a preview of an irrelevant set reduces the influence of the irrelevant set on search efficiency, but only when the number of irrelevant set elements is large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subset selective search in a preview condition is not a unitary phenomenon but rather a function of the specific conditions of the task.
the number of relevant and irrelevant elements should be manipulated independently to disentangle their respective contributions to search efficiency.
the effect of a color difference on preview search is not a general phenomenon but is dependent on the type of feature conjunction that defines the target.
